cells.tense: Right now you are steering and seeing clearly and both are yours.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you have been circling and tell someone what you see — once, plainly, no case built.
cells.core:
You can see the shape of a thing and still steer by it. That is rarer than either half. Lots of people read a room; fewer can read it and then say this way, not that one, and mean it. You have both running at once right now, and it is why your choices tend to land where you aimed them.

The shape you are seeing is not finished, and you are not pretending it is. Knowing like this keeps deepening the longer you stand in it. The one place it can go stiff is when what you see starts to feel like a verdict — including on yourself. So pick one thing you keep circling and say what you see out loud, once, to one person. No case, no hedge. What you set down, you get to keep.
cells.sheetLine: You can see the whole thing and still choose. That is working.
cells.verb: seeing the whole pattern while standing inside it
cells.place: at the helm, saying this and not that

cells.tense: You are deciding what all of this means before it has finished happening.
cells.ask: Hold back the verdict on one person for a week; when the judgement forms, say only what you observed and nothing about what it proves.
cells.core:
You are ahead of the moment, already scoring it. Every situation gets read fast and filed under what it really is, and what you find is starting to arrive as a verdict — on other people, on yourself. From the outside it looks like certainty. From inside it costs something: you are judging from above the room instead of standing in it.

Seeing the pattern is a real gift, and right now it is running past what the moment can carry. The way back is not more insight; it is direction you actually choose. So give one person a week without a verdict. When the judgement forms, say what you saw — the action, the words — and stop before you say what it proves.

cells.tense: A call came and you stayed seated, and part of you is still waiting by that door.
cells.ask: Say one plain sentence about what you notice, to one person, before you feel ready.
cells.core:
You look at the whole of something and it does not lead anywhere. There is another source to check, another angle, another conversation to have first — and what you see does not resolve into a choice. That much reading, and still no direction, is what this corner of your life feels like from where you sit.

What is missing is not more information. It is one small, real act of your own, taken fresh, with nothing settled beforehand. This is not a decision to get right; it is a direction to step into and let the next step show itself. Pick one person and say one plain sentence about what you notice, while it is still half-formed. That is the charge this part of you runs on.

cells.tense: You are already steering this and talking about it like weather.
cells.ask: Name one call you have already made and say aloud that it was yours.
cells.core:
You have been choosing, and the pattern is there to see, and you act on it — while describing the whole thing as if it were happening to you. Situations unfold, people change, things shake out. The calls you make do not get named, so they do not get counted.

What is missing is credit, given to the right party. Not congratulations — fairness. When your own calls go uncounted, the ledger runs crooked and you start feeling owed without knowing why. Take one decision you have already made and say, out loud, that it was yours. No rehearsal needed. You are already doing this; the only change is saying so.
